reviews.review: This game is not good, but it still has an odd draw to it. It's good if you like some B grade ass games. Just DO NOT buy at full price. Wait for a deep sale.

[strike]I wish there were an indifferent choice rather than just a yes or no when writing reviews. I am enjoying the game and will most likely continue on through the game. However a few of my major concerns deal with the overall polish of the game especially with it having been out for a full year. First off is my gripe with the lock on. When you get to close to an enemy you can actually get stuck and your strafing seems to become diabled, I have died plenty of times due to this. Another major issue that I have run into as well as seen in other reviews is the fact then when enemies rush you, you will shoot right through them dealing no damage. I have also run into a variety of UI issues that either force me to return to the main menu and then get back into the game, or out right exit the application, haveing to relaunch it to continue playing. 
The UI issues that I have run deal with:
- ammo count becoming frozen
- Loadout slots overlapping one another when trying to equip weapons
- Scrapping becoming unavailable despite having the weapon unlocked for scrapping purposes
- No longer being able to select any but the current gun you have equipped in the load out screen

Other issues I have run into deal with the combat and these are:
- No longer being able to fire forcing the player to swap guns and then back to the original to be able to continue firing
- Character positon becoming locked when player is locked onto an enemy that either the player gets to close to or the enemy gets to close to the player 
- Enemies attacks tracking player position after animation is playered or during animation (I.E. Enemy leap strikes and player dodges out of the way. Enemy then while mid air does a 180 turn and lands the strike on the player)

Other issues are minor and are more or less preferences that I would have liked to have seen such as item use cancelation with a dodge or other small quality of life improvements. 

I will keep my eye on the future development of the game, I would really like to be able to recommend this game to fans of other souls games as it is clear this games had a lot of influence from others inthe genre. If any of the aformentioned issued end up being resolved I will change the recommendation.[/strike]

Edit: Having kept my eye on the development of the game for a while now I would like to come back to this review and change my recommendation. I did thoroughly enjoy myself while playing through this. In fact I played through one save nearly 5 times.

So I finished the game and I can say I recommend it. But you must be aware this is not Dark Souls, with that in mind, you should be able to write a fair review. 

To the people complaining about difficulty: Seriously? Yeah, I died, a lot, but that was because I went Rambo full ♥♥♥♥♥♥ charge style, this game doesn't work like that, you must take your time and take down enemies one by one. If you get hit from multiple angles at the same time, and you can't run for cover, you'll certainly die. Be careful when fighting strong melee enemies, if knocked down, you'll certainly die. See that trap hiding in a shrub over there? Remember it, because if you're running from an ambush and step on it, you'll certainly die. You'll have fun anywhere (I'm not being sarcastic).

The game was pretty good for me, it hooked me enough to finished it and that's an achievement by itself. I have a lot of unfinished games because they bored me. 

Pros:
- Good visuals, especially the levels (for the price, of course, they could be better)
- The lore and story. There's a point where it feels cliche, but believe me, it's not. There's a little surprise by the end, which I think is a pretty nice detail from developers.
- Difficulty. This game challenges you a lot, but as you can read in the comments, it's not for everyone. If you get easily frustrated, stay away.

But the game has flaws, and must be mentioned because I hope they get removed in a future sequel:

- Animations. At some points, they feel cheap. Dead animations could be better, and lengthier (they feel rushed at some point). Story animations could be done in the engine
- The bosses. We need to have some variety, and we're missing some large creatures (there were some giant bug-like machine props in a graveyard level, they could've been fun to fight against), and we're missing multiple phases, some have them, but not very noticeable (we need some transformations, especially final bosses).
- Weapon balancing. Actually, the game forces you to select a specific type of weapon as your main: sniper rifles. That's because it's the strongest type, but it shouldn't. Shotguns, for example, should be stronger in close range (they're strong,  but sometimes, I preferred to spend sniper rifle ammunition to kill annoying enemies, because it's faster).

This game is pretty much like Dark Souls with guns, but there are a few differences. Enemies and bosses are hard as expected but there are way too many annoying traps and checkpoints are VERY rare. Imagine going through 3-4 major areas of Dark Souls without any bonfires, you will have to repeat the same content a lot if you aren't careful with your potions. Many times you will run out of ammo too and ammo packs drops are very rare. You won't be able to use most of the guns you find because they require very different stats depending on your build. You won't be able to lock-on often either, because you will have to take down a lot of enemies from a distance, where lock-on is not possible. I didn't enjoy this game and progressed only 3/8 so far, my main issue with the game is the lack of checkpoints.

If you are a Dark Souls fan like me and looking for a similar game, try Salt and Sanctuary, which is still the best souls-like.

The typical Souls type of game: you kill, accumulate [i]souls[/i], and spend those [i]souls[/i] to upgrade your eight attributes. No problem here. I love the elemental effects on the guns--I have a blast spamming the fire submachine uzi! The main problem is the logic of the game. Each of your weapons have a range stat. [b]However, the NPCs do not![/b] They can shoot you from a mile away! Even equipping a sniper does nothing! Your reticle must turn red in order to register hits, but you must first be within a certain distance (think thirty feet/nine meters IRL!) to get that red reticle! What kind of failure is this?!  

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1594927059 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1594927367 

Another problem's the placement of the traps, and there are a plethora. Some are hidden in dense foliage so it's hard to see them until it's too late. Some are placed within sight, but as to why they're literally spammed across the map is very poor design! You'll do best to tiptoe around them until NPCs come running towards you. Looks like the dev did it that way to meet a quota. 

Instances of NPCs spawning out of nowhere are unfair. You can actually see them spawn when you cross that trigger threshold. I cleared an area getting ready to fight a guy with a shield/sword. Right as I aggro him I got hit from an enemy from behind; after a couple of tests that enemy always spawns in the area I had already cleared when I trigger like walking past a certain distance. I enjoy being cautious and concentrating intently around the environment for nasties like in Dark Souls. I feel satisfaction when I know what's before me and plan in advance of what's going to be necessary in order to progress forward. 

Stealth is broken. Supressors usually attract NPCs after a one shot kill. Pointless to have them. 

Although not as glamorous to the Dark Souls 2 environments, the artwork's quite beautiful as are the environments! The layout of the maps is pretty nice--you have the opportunity to find shortcuts to [i]bonfires[/i] and alternative routes. The voice acting's great! 

The NPCs are sometimes near each other you'll use melee very sparingly; you'll discover assigning [i]souls[/i] to the melee attribute won't really benefit you since most of the journey will inevitably involve gun warfare. Consequently, ammo drops from the NPCs would've been a QOL feature (ammo drops are very rare); I've had to return to the last [i]bonfire[/i] to replenish ammo. 

The elemental effects for ranged/melee weapons are eye candy. Very titi||ating spamming my flame uzi or poison shotgun! 

The [i]bonfires[/i] are placed fairly. 

The gun souls is a unique, fun feature, but I can't recommend this game because of the point about the stupid range fail which is riotously essential for gun combat. Of course, melee combat exists, but gun combat takes the icing here. 

So, why do I have 41 hours? I'm patient enough to not mind the range limit and the gun combat has me returning. It's a really good game if you can be like me =]] but such cons can become a thorn in your side when you play.

I love dark souls so I ignored the other bad reviews and picked this up. That was a mistake. There are many elements of this game that don't seem to work well. The targeting in particular is bad. It is very easy to miss targets that are too close even when they are fully in your reticle. Several times some bug caused me to fire endlessly or to not fire at all for a duration and requied me to play around with the game until it would work again. The save locations aren't particularly great. It is pretty common to get attacked immediately upon leaving the save area. One particular area leaves you vulnerable to to 5 enemies that rush you in a small area. If you save there it is difficult just to be able to escape the area. I repeatedly had to restart 5 feet from my body. There are other areas that are basically long straight paths that leave you vulnerable to fire from enemies that can infinitely spam shields on the ground that allow them to fire through but block damage the other way. At a couple points in the game the makers decide to place these traps that root you with suicide enemies. There are probably about 50 of the traps in one area. That is just way too many. Some areas have infinitely spawning suicide enemies. There are many enemies with silly hitboxes, especially the ones that rush you. They hit you long before they should and many of them will kill you either in one hit with the charge or finish you off while you are stunned on the ground from the charge. It seems like they kept every unfun element of dark souls while taking away the fun and the feeling of accomplishment.

I will do a quick first impression review since i see alot of mixed reviews recently. 
While writing this im on the forest world and got about 4 hours of time in the game. 

Comparing this to dark souls is abit unfair, however it is souls-like in my opinion. It is more of the first dark souls (not remastered) which when compared to the 3rd game is like playing in slow-motion, not the same fastpaced action. 

My first impression is a good one, the game has a slow and steady pace and you start out in a tutorial setting which gives you the basics of movement and combat. However alot of things are left unexplained, for instance the attributes, what to level up first (ring a bell, souls-fans?). 
The combat is abit sluggish, yes. However it's hard to incorporate ranged combat in a "souls-like" game without becoming too shoot-em-up. The game is challenging and i can agree on the frustration of environmental hazards, there are no indication of what is a regular bush and what will bite your leg off. 

The setting is familiar to those who played the souls series, you die and go back to a safe spot called Obelisks ("bonfires"), and you lose the bits (souls) at the spot you died. 
I got the game at 24.99 EURO and so far i would recommend getting it on sale as the full price is abit steep. 
The short first impression gives me roughly the same "unpolished gem" feeling the first dark souls gave me, however it might be too early to say as it might turn out to become a guilded turd in the end, in which case i will do a new review. 

TL;DR 
Challenging, slow-paced souls-like game. Died to a shrub GG.
